```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chiriac_2024_dalbavancin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chiriac_2024_dalbavancin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics13111103>
* Supplement (Tables S1-S5, Figures S1-S3): <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/antibiotics13111103/s1>

Chiriac 2024 fitted 38 total serum dalbavancin concentrations from 13 men with
a persistent ventricular assist device (VAD) driveline infection who received
dalbavancin as long-term suppressive outpatient therapy (1500 mg on days 1 and
8, repeated every 6 weeks). The final Monolix model is a two-compartment
intravenous model with intercompartmental clearance fixed to a previously
published value (Buckwalter 2005) and log-normal random effects on CL, V1 and
V2. None of the six screened covariates (BSA, albumin, body weight, age, serum
creatinine, creatinine clearance) was retained; they are documented in the
model's `covariatesDataExcluded` metadata. The paper then simulated six
regimens and computed the probability of target attainment (PTA) for
`fAUC24h/MIC > 27.1` (stasis) under protein-binding scenarios of 93-99%.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chiriac_2024_dalbavancin"))$population
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Field = c("Subjects", "Observations", "Age", "Weight", "Female (%)",
              "Renal function", "Disease", "Dosing", "Regions"),
    Value = c(pop$n_subjects, pop$n_observations, pop$age_range,
              pop$weight_range, pop$sex_female_pct, pop$renal_function,
              pop$disease_state, pop$dose_range, pop$regions)
  ),
  caption = "Chiriac 2024 study population (Results 2.1, Table 1, Methods 4.1)."
)
```

All 13 patients were men with a HeartMate III device; the mean body surface
area was 1.95 m^2 and the mean creatinine clearance 90.8 mL/min (Table 1).
Total-dalbavancin protein binding measured in the cohort was 96-98%, above the
93% of the product label.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | log(0.050 L/h) | Table 2, CL (RSE 6.83%) |
| `lvc` | log(6.5 L) | Table 2, V1 (RSE 8.05%) |
| `lq` | fixed(log(0.476 L/h)) | Table 2, Q (no RSE); Results 2.2 'fixed intercompartmental clearance (Q), based on a previous reported value' |
| `lvp` | log(15.4 L) | Table 2, V2 (RSE 12.3%) |
| `etalcl` | 0.0529 (= 0.230^2) | Table 2, omega CL = 0.230 (Monolix SD of the log-normal random effect) |
| `etalvc` | 0.0676 (= 0.260^2) | Table 2, omega V1 = 0.260 |
| `etalvp` | 0.1681 (= 0.410^2) | Table 2, omega V2 = 0.410 |
| `propSd` | 0.100 | Table 2, b (proportional residual error) |
| Two-compartment IV structure | n/a | Results 2.2; Supplement Table S1 (CL, V1, V2, Q fixed) |
| `Cc = central / vc` (total serum dalbavancin) | n/a | Results 2.2 'developed for the total dalbavancin serum concentrations' |
| `fAUC24h = (1 - PB) x AUC24h` over the last 24 h before redosing | n/a | Methods 4.3; Supplement Table S5 footnote |

# Typical-value check against the observed concentrations

Results 2.1 reports the observed total concentrations after the
day-1/day-8 regimen: 218.4 +/- 65.9 mg/L 30 min after the end of the first
infusion, 41.1 +/- 11.1 mg/L before the day-8 dose and 13.2 +/- 9.9 mg/L after
6 weeks (before the next cycle). The infusion duration is not reported; the
30-minute infusion of the product label is assumed throughout.

```{r d1d8-cohort}
mod <- readModelDb("Chiriac_2024_dalbavancin")
week <- 168
inf_dur <- 0.5

obs_times <- c(inf_dur + 0.5, week - 0.1, 6 * week - 0.1)
ev_d1d8 <- rxode2::et(amt = 1500, dur = inf_dur, time = c(0, week), cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(time = obs_times, cmt = "central")

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241103)
sim_d1d8 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_d1d8, nSub = 200) |> as.data.frame()
typ_d1d8 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_d1d8) |> as.data.frame()

obs_check <- tibble::tibble(
  time = obs_times,
  Sample = c("30 min after end of 1st infusion", "Day 8, before 2nd dose", "Week 6, before next cycle"),
  obs_mean = c(218.4, 41.1, 13.2),
  obs_sd = c(65.9, 11.1, 9.9)
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim_d1d8 |>
      dplyr::group_by(time) |>
      dplyr::summarise(sim_mean = mean(Cc), sim_sd = sd(Cc), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "time"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(typ_d1d8 |> dplyr::select(time, typical = Cc), by = "time") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_mean - obs_mean) / obs_mean)

obs_check |>
  dplyr::select(-time) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Observed mean (mg/L)" = obs_mean,
    "Observed SD" = obs_sd,
    "Simulated mean (mg/L)" = sim_mean,
    "Simulated SD" = sim_sd,
    "Typical value (mg/L)" = typical,
    "Mean difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Observed (Results 2.1) vs. simulated total dalbavancin, 200 virtual patients on 1500 mg days 1 and 8.")

# The first two samples are well above the 12.5 mg/L quantification limit, so
# the observed means are unbiased; a 200-patient mean has a standard error of
# about 2-3% of its value here, so 20% leaves room for the 13-patient observed
# mean's own uncertainty while a wrong volume or dose unit moves it far more.
stopifnot(all(abs(obs_check$pct_diff[1:2]) < 20))
```

The end-of-infusion and day-8 concentrations agree with the observed means
within a few percent. At week 6 the simulated mean sits above the observed
13.2 mg/L. The week-6 concentrations lie close to the 12.5 mg/L quantification
limit, and Methods 4.2 replaced below-limit values with half the limit
(6.25 mg/L), which pulls the observed mean down; this comparison is therefore
not gated.

# Replicate Supplement Table S5 (individual AUC24h)

Supplement Table S5 lists every patient's empirical-Bayes CL, V1 and V2 and the
total-dalbavancin AUC over the last 24 h before redosing. Table S5 does not say
which redose. Solving each patient's printed parameters through the packaged
model shows that the tabulated AUC is the one before the **third** cycle, i.e.
after two 6-week cycles of 1500 mg on days 1 and 8 (`2 x 1008 h`). Because both
sides use the same individual parameters, this is a tight deterministic check
of the structure and of the fixed Q.

```{r table-s5}
s5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~cl,   ~v1,   ~v2,   ~mic,  ~pb,  ~auc24, ~fauc_mic,
  1L,  0.067, 10.84, 21.11, 0.064, 97.6, 377,    141,
  2L,  0.056, 7.07,  34.97, 0.064, 96.7, 616,    318,
  3L,  0.059, 5.17,  12.34, NA,    97.0, 216,    26,
  4L,  0.033, 6.23,  24.73, NA,    97.2, 1138,   127,
  5L,  0.046, 5.25,  16.48, 0.094, 98.1, 547,    110,
  6L,  0.052, 8.68,  13.65, NA,    97.1, 429,    49,
  7L,  0.070, 6.93,  19.04, 0.047, 97.1, 267,    165,
  8L,  0.056, 8.30,  11.70, 0.047, 96.2, 313,    253,
  9L,  0.032, 4.44,  15.01, 0.064, 96.2, 980,    582,
  10L, 0.047, 6.58,  9.45,  0.125, 97.8, 341,    60,
  11L, 0.050, 6.34,  18.24, 0.064, 96.2, 524,    311,
  12L, 0.050, 5.52,  11.53, 0.047, 98.5, 326,    104,
  13L, 0.057, 5.77,  9.04,  0.064, 96.8, 168,    84
)

cycle <- 6 * week
s5_doses <- c(0, week, cycle, cycle + week)
s5_end <- 2 * cycle
ev_s5 <- rxode2::et(amt = 1500, dur = inf_dur, time = s5_doses, cmt = "central", id = s5$id) |>
  rxode2::et(time = seq(s5_end - 24, s5_end, by = 1), cmt = "central", id = s5$id)

# One row of individual parameters per patient, in id order. zeroRe() removes
# the random effects, so rxode2 notes a multi-subject solve without omega.
s5_params <- data.frame(id = s5$id, lcl = log(s5$cl), lvc = log(s5$v1), lvp = log(s5$v2))
sim_s5 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_s5, params = s5_params) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  sim_s5 |> dplyr::distinct(id, cl) |> dplyr::pull(cl), s5$cl
)))

conc_s5 <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_s5 |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | id)
dose_s5 <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = s5$id, time = s5_doses) |> dplyr::mutate(amt = 1500),
  amt ~ time | id
)
nca_s5 <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_s5, dose_s5,
  intervals = data.frame(start = s5_end - 24, end = s5_end, auclast = TRUE)
))

s5_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_s5,
  reference = s5 |> dplyr::select(id, auclast = auc24),
  by = "id",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 5
)
knitr::kable(s5_cmp, caption = "AUC over the last 24 h before the third cycle: packaged model with each patient's Table S5 parameters vs. Table S5 AUC24h. * differs by >5%.")

auc_s5 <- as.data.frame(nca_s5) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(id, auc_sim = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(s5, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_diff = 100 * (auc_sim - auc24) / auc24,
    # Table S5 footnote: a missing MIC was replaced with the 0.25 mg/L breakpoint.
    fauc_mic_sim = auc_sim * (1 - pb / 100) / dplyr::coalesce(mic, 0.25)
  )
stopifnot(nrow(auc_s5) == 13L)
# Deterministic: both sides use the same parameters, so the only difference is
# the 2-3 significant figures Table S5 prints them to (measured within 1.4%).
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_s5$pct_diff) < 3))
```

```{r table-s5-fauc, echo = FALSE}
auc_s5 |>
  dplyr::select(id, pb, mic, fauc_mic, fauc_mic_sim) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Patient" = id,
    "Protein binding (%)" = pb,
    "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
    "fAUC24h/MIC, Table S5" = fauc_mic,
    "fAUC24h/MIC, model" = fauc_mic_sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 1, 3, 0, 0), caption = "fAUC24h/MIC per patient (Table S5; a missing MIC uses the 0.25 mg/L breakpoint).")
```

# Dosing simulations (Figures 3 and 4)

Methods 4.3 lists the six simulated regimens. Each is simulated here for 200
virtual patients over the 12 weeks shown in Figure 3.

```{r regimens}
regimens <- list(
  "1000 mg q2 weeks" = list(amt = 1000, doses = seq(0, 10, by = 2) * week, end = 12 * week),
  "1500 mg q3 weeks" = list(amt = 1500, doses = seq(0, 9, by = 3) * week, end = 12 * week),
  "1500 mg q4 weeks" = list(amt = 1500, doses = seq(0, 8, by = 4) * week, end = 12 * week),
  "1500 mg q5 weeks" = list(amt = 1500, doses = c(0, 5) * week, end = 10 * week),
  "1500 mg day 1 day 8 q6 weeks" = list(amt = 1500, doses = c(0, 1, 6, 7) * week, end = 12 * week),
  "1500 mg day 1 day 15 q6 weeks" = list(amt = 1500, doses = c(0, 2, 6, 8) * week, end = 12 * week)
)

simulate_regimen <- function(name, reg, n = 200L) {
  # Doses after `end` belong only to Figure 3's display window.
  plot_doses <- if (reg$end < 12 * week) c(reg$doses, reg$end) else reg$doses
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = reg$amt, dur = inf_dur, time = plot_doses, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(
      time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12 * week, by = 6), seq(reg$end - 24, reg$end, by = 1)))),
      cmt = "central"
    )
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, nSub = n) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::rename(id = sim.id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = name, window_end = reg$end)
}

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241104)
sim_reg <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(regimens), function(nm) simulate_regimen(nm, regimens[[nm]])))
sim_reg$regimen <- factor(sim_reg$regimen, levels = names(regimens))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_reg$Cc))
```

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6}
sim_reg |>
  dplyr::filter(time %% 6 == 0, time > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / week, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 400)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 12, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Weeks", y = "Total dalbavancin (mg/L)",
    title = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles by regimen",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Chiriac 2024."
  )
```

The PK/PD index is the free AUC over the last 24 h before redosing (Methods
4.3). The AUC is taken here before the last redose inside the 12-week window
(week 12, or week 10 for the 5-week interval) and computed with PKNCA.

```{r pta-nca}
win <- sim_reg |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= window_end - 24, time <= window_end, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, id, time, Cc)

dose_reg <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(regimens), function(nm) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(200L), time = regimens[[nm]]$doses) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = nm, amt = regimens[[nm]]$amt)
}))
dose_reg$regimen <- factor(dose_reg$regimen, levels = names(regimens))

intervals_reg <- tibble::tibble(
  regimen = factor(names(regimens), levels = names(regimens)),
  start = vapply(regimens, function(r) r$end - 24, numeric(1)),
  end = vapply(regimens, function(r) r$end, numeric(1)),
  auclast = TRUE
)

nca_reg <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(win, Cc ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_reg, amt ~ time | regimen + id),
  intervals = intervals_reg
))
auc_reg <- as.data.frame(nca_reg) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, id, auc24 = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(auc_reg) == 6L * 200L, !anyNA(auc_reg$auc24))

mics <- c(0.016, 0.032, 0.064, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2)
pta <- tidyr::expand_grid(auc_reg, pb = 93:99, mic = mics) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, pb, mic) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta = 100 * mean(auc24 * (1 - pb / 100) / mic > 27.1), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(pta, aes(factor(mic), pta, colour = factor(pb), group = factor(pb))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(shape = 15) +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA fAUC24h/MIC > 27.1 (%)", colour = "PB (%)",
    title = "Probability of target attainment for stasis",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Chiriac 2024."
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

The PTA values below were digitised by the maintainers from Figure 4 at the
two extreme protein-binding scenarios, on the steep part of each curve where
the comparison is informative.

```{r figure-4-compare}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,                         ~pb, ~mic,  ~pta_paper,
  "1000 mg q2 weeks",               99,  0.25,  85,
  "1000 mg q2 weeks",               99,  0.5,   12,
  "1000 mg q2 weeks",               93,  2,     75,
  "1500 mg q3 weeks",               99,  0.125, 96,
  "1500 mg q3 weeks",               99,  0.25,  66,
  "1500 mg q3 weeks",               93,  1,     94,
  "1500 mg q3 weeks",               93,  2,     53,
  "1500 mg q4 weeks",               99,  0.125, 76,
  "1500 mg q4 weeks",               99,  0.25,  21,
  "1500 mg q4 weeks",               93,  1,     68,
  "1500 mg q4 weeks",               93,  2,     12,
  "1500 mg q5 weeks",               99,  0.064, 82,
  "1500 mg q5 weeks",               99,  0.125, 45,
  "1500 mg q5 weeks",               93,  0.5,   78,
  "1500 mg q5 weeks",               93,  1,     35,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 8 q6 weeks",   99,  0.064, 92,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 8 q6 weeks",   99,  0.125, 73,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 8 q6 weeks",   99,  0.25,  28,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 8 q6 weeks",   93,  1,     67,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 8 q6 weeks",   93,  2,     20,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 15 q6 weeks",  99,  0.125, 86,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 15 q6 weeks",  99,  0.25,  43,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 15 q6 weeks",  93,  1,     81,
  "1500 mg day 1 day 15 q6 weeks",  93,  2,     32
)
fig4_cmp <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens))) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(pta, by = c("regimen", "pb", "mic")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = pta - pta_paper)
stopifnot(nrow(fig4_cmp) == nrow(fig4))

fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "PB (%)" = pb, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
    "PTA, Figure 4 (%)" = pta_paper, "PTA, model (%)" = pta,
    "Difference (points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 3, 0, 0, 0), caption = "PTA for stasis: digitised Figure 4 vs. 200 simulated patients per regimen.")

# A PTA from 200 patients has a binomial SE of up to 3.5 points, the
# digitisation about 2 points; a 20% error in CL or V shifts the steep part of
# these curves by 20-40 points. Centre and robust envelope, not the worst row.
stopifnot(
  median(abs(fig4_cmp$diff)) < 8,
  quantile(abs(fig4_cmp$diff), 0.9) < 20
)

# Results 2.3: at 99% protein binding and the 0.125 mg/L ECOFF, only 1000 mg
# q2 weeks and 1500 mg q3 weeks reach PTA >= 90%. The two passing regimens sit
# at about 95-100% and the best failing one near 80%, each several binomial SEs
# from the 90% line.
pta_ecoff <- pta |> dplyr::filter(pb == 99, mic == 0.125)
stopifnot(nrow(pta_ecoff) == 6L)
passing <- as.character(pta_ecoff$regimen[pta_ecoff$pta >= 90])
stopifnot(setequal(passing, c("1000 mg q2 weeks", "1500 mg q3 weeks")))
```

The simulated curves follow Figure 4, and the paper's headline result is
reproduced: at 99% protein binding and an MIC of 0.125 mg/L only 1000 mg every
2 weeks and 1500 mg every 3 weeks keep the PTA at or above 90% (Results 2.3).
The simulated PTA sits 1-10 points below the digitised values throughout, most
for the 5-week interval. That regimen has only one complete interval before
its week-10 redose; when the same calculation is moved to later intervals of a
longer dose train, its PTA at 99% binding and 0.125 mg/L rises from about 37%
towards 42%, closer to the figure's 45%. The paper's PTA was therefore
probably evaluated nearer steady state than the 12 weeks plotted in Figure 3,
which the paper does not state.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Infusion duration.** Not reported; the 30-minute infusion of the product
  label is assumed. It affects only the first hour after each dose.
- **Monolix omega scale.** Table 2 reports omega for CL, V1 and V2 as Monolix
  does, as the standard deviation of the log-normal random effect; the
  packaged variances are omega squared.
- **Fixed Q.** Q = 0.476 L/h is fixed in the source (Results 2.2, Table 2 with
  no RSE) to the value of Buckwalter 2005 and is encoded with `fixed()`. No IIV
  on Q is reported.
- **Albumin unit.** Table 1 prints albumin as 42.5 +/- 5.7 'mg/dL'; the value
  is physiologically g/L. Albumin was not retained in the model.
- **Table S5 redose.** Table S5 does not say before which redose its AUC24h
  was taken; the AUC before the third 6-week cycle reproduces all 13 rows
  within 1.5%, so that reading is used. One patient received 1000 mg instead
  of 1500 mg (Results 2.1) but is not identified; every patient is simulated
  at 1500 mg, and all 13 rows still agree.
- **PTA window.** The AUC window for Figure 4 is taken before the last redose
  inside the 12-week window of Figure 3. The paper does not state the
  simulation horizon for the PTA; see the comment under the Figure 4
  comparison.
- **Figure 5 (cumulative fraction of response).** Not replicated: it weights
  the PTA curves by the EUCAST S. aureus dalbavancin MIC distribution, which
  the paper cites but does not print.
- **Week-6 trough.** The simulated mean week-6 concentration exceeds the
  observed mean of 13.2 mg/L; the observed value is depressed by the
  half-quantification-limit imputation of below-limit samples (Methods 4.2).
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (EuropePMC
  search, 2026-10-31).
